facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative

support_spans: Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy and tissue culture results are consistent with cutaneous cryptococcosis, and the presence of a tender nodule on the forehead supports this diagnosis.
The patient's low lymphocyte count and treatment with fingolimod, an immunosuppressive medication, increase the risk of opportunistic infections like cryptococcosis.

rationales.F02: Fingolimod treatment increases the risk of opportunistic infections, including cryptococcosis.
rationales.F06: The presence of an eroded, crusted papule is a characteristic skin lesion of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F10: The skin biopsy result showing granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules is diagnostic of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F11: The growth of Cryptococcus neoformans in tissue culture confirms the diagnosis of cutaneous cryptococcosis.
rationales.F12: The negative HIV test result reduces the likelihood of immunodeficiency-associated cryptococcosis.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of granulomatous inflammation and narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules in the skin biopsy, along with the eroded, crusted papule on the forehead, specifically supports Cutaneous Cryptococcosis.
